title: Wales 20 mph Casualty Attribution Audit: A Constructive Non-Identification Result
oneLine: The first-year casualty decline is descriptively reproducible, but the frozen aggregate evidence identifies neither the point value nor the sign of the policy effect on affected roads.
abstract: A provisional Welsh Government graphic reported 2,402 casualties on roads recorded as 20 or 30 mph in the four-quarter baseline and 1,725 in the first four complete post-implementation quarters, an exact decline of about 28.18%. This source-bound audit reproduces that historical comparison and preserves later official vintages, then separates the combined posted-speed proxy from the causal estimand on road segments whose speed limit actually changed. The frozen corpus contains neither a versioned historical treatment map nor an observed no-policy outcome for affected roads. A deterministic constructive witness holds the same aggregate observables fixed while hypothetical affected-road counterfactuals imply effects of -50%, 0% and +100%. The values are counterexamples, not estimates or bounds. Within the registered corpus and rival class, neither the causal point nor its sign is identified; the positive 28% attribution remains unsupported. The result does not establish that the policy worked, failed or had no effect.
narration: Wales reported a large first-year fall in police-recorded casualties on roads marked 20 or 30 miles per hour. This audit reproduces the provisional comparison: 2,402 casualties before and 1,725 after, about 28 percent lower. But that aggregate does not identify the causal effect of the policy on roads whose speed limit actually changed. The published series mixes affected roads with roads that were already 20, retained at 30, or later reverted. The frozen evidence also lacks the affected roads' unobserved no-policy outcome. The package therefore constructs three hypothetical worlds with exactly the same observed aggregate totals but negative, zero and positive effects on affected roads. These worlds are counterexamples, not estimates or bounds. They show that, within the registered corpus and rival class, neither the point value nor even the sign of the policy effect is identified. This unrefereed candidate does not say that the policy worked, failed or had no effect. The full records, sources, code and producer-side replay evidence are linked. This is an AI-generated communication summary and is not additional policy evidence.

keyResults: The provisional source statistic reconstructs exactly from 2,402 to 1,725 casualties, or about -28.18%, but it is a before/after comparison on the combined 20/30 mph class rather than the registered affected-road causal estimand.
Later frozen routes are not numerically invariant: the current StatsWales extract gives about -26.10%, while the current DfT collision-row diagnostic gives about -24.18%.
The corpus lacks both a versioned historical map of affected road segments and the affected roads' no-policy post outcome.

Three hypothetical worlds reproduce the same aggregate observables while implying affected-road effects of -50%, 0% and +100%; they establish corpus-specific point-and-sign non-identification but are not estimates or bounds.
The positive 28% causal attribution remains unsupported, and no zero, beneficial, harmful or otherwise signed policy effect is reported.
